docs.title: TwinCat-MCP
docs.text:
MCP server for TwinCAT 3 PLC development. Let AI coding agents — Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor — build, configure, deploy, and debug TwinCAT PLC projects through a standard tool interface.

Download TwinCat-MCP Get started Connect your agent

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: TwinCat-MCP runs as a Windows Service exposing a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint. A TcXaeShell plugin bridges the TwinCAT Automation Interface, so an agent can create POUs, manage libraries, build, activate configurations, and read/write PLC variables over ADS — all programmatically.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 56 MCP tools across project, build, system, and runtime operations.
  • Works with your agent — Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor.
  • Live PLC interaction — read/write symbols and browse the running PLC via ADS.
  • Safe by default — UserMode Runtime and guarded operations for risky actions.

docs.title: [0.2.0-beta.1] - 2026-11-12
docs.text:
TwinCat-MCP now runs as a Windows Service with a TcXaeShell Plugin, installed from one MSI package. Agents connect over Streamable HTTP. The tool set grows from 44 to 56 tools, and the software is licensed per machine.

Beta

The beta MSI is not code-signed yet. See Installation for how to check the download.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• MSI installer with two features, MCP Service and TcXaeShell Plugin: a setup wizard with the license agreement, prerequisite checks, an option to close a running TcXaeShell, and unattended installs (ADDLOCAL, CLOSETCXAESHELL=1). See Installation.
  • Upgrade in place that keeps settings and license; uninstall keeps %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP unless PURGEDATA=1 is passed.
  • Setup reports a taken HTTP port and the program that holds it; the Service starts on the port once it is free.
  • Streamable HTTP transport: the MCP endpoint is served at POST /mcp on localhost:3001 by a Windows Service. It replaces the previous stdio console app.
  • TcXaeShell Plugin, to which the Service routes the project tools.
  • quit_instance: close a TcXaeShell instance.
  • scan_io_devices: scan I/O devices on the target.
  • scan_plc_project: discover the PLC project tree with type labels.
  • read_item_xml / write_item_xml: read and write the XML configuration of any tree node.
  • link_variables / unlink_variables: create and remove I/O variable mappings.
  • get_umr_netid: get the UserMode Runtime AMS NetId.
  • search: fuzzy or regex search across POUs, DUTs, GVLs, symbols and hardware, including live ADS symbols.
  • project_digest: a one-call project overview of POUs, DUTs, GVLs, libraries and tasks.
  • read_pou_batch: read several POUs in one call.
  • check_objects: validate configuration objects.
  • service_memory: show the Service's memory use and limits, and release unused memory on request.
  • MCP resources: twincat://{instanceId}/tree, /pous, /libraries.
  • dryRun preview for the mutating tools write_pou, write_item_xml, delete_item, rename_item, link_variables and unlink_variables.
  • Offline, machine-bound licensing with get_license_status, generate_license_request and install_license. See Licensing.
  • Options window with tabbed pages: General, Safety, Connection, UMR, Licensing, Memory & Limits, Help and About, with recommended default instructions for agents.
  • Memory & Limits page with a live memory bar, and the BrowseSymbolsMaxNodes and MaxPrivateMemoryMB settings. See Configuration.
  • A memory guard and automatic memory release in the Service.
  • Copy-reference context menu in the Plugin.
  • Standard License Agreement, shown by the installer, and a Trial License Agreement for evaluations.
  • THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, installed with the software.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Architecture: the single console app (stdio) is replaced by a Windows Service (MCP and ADS) plus a TcXaeShell Plugin.
  • The Service is self-contained; no separate .NET runtime is needed.
  • Starting and stopping the UserMode Runtime moved into the Plugin: the six target-changing tools take useUmr=true, or need confirmed=true on other targets.
  • Read tools gained parameters such as fields that limit the size of the output.
  • Tool descriptions steer agents toward the search and file tools, which saves tokens.
  • Structured, machine-readable error codes across tools.
  • Reached limits are reported as notices ("Limit reached, not an error"), not as errors.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• attach and attach_by_process_id: launch_instance reuses a running instance.
  • start_umr and stop_umr: replaced by the useUmr parameter.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• launch_instance handles invalid solution paths, and starts TcXaeShell in the signed-in user's session.
  • create_pou creates interface methods, properties and their accessors with the correct types.
  • PLC compile errors are reported as errors and fail build.
  • browse_symbols and symbol search no longer walk the whole symbol tree, which caused very high Service memory use. maxDepth now defaults to 2, with new maxNodes and followPointers parameters.
  • Lower Service memory use under load.
  • The Options window scrolls with the mouse wheel.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The UserMode Runtime and all tools require a valid license; only the three licensing tools work without one.
  • Only SYSTEM and administrators can change the license folder.

docs.text:
• list_instances — list running TcXaeShell and Visual Studio instances.
  • attach — attach to a running instance by solution name.
  • attach_by_process_id — attach to a running instance by PID.

docs.title: POU Management
docs.text:
• create_pou — create any IEC 61131-3 POU type (Program, Function, FB, Method, Property, DUT, GVL, Interface).
  • read_pou — read declaration and implementation, with a recursive mode for full FB/Interface trees.
  • write_pou — write declaration and/or implementation in a single call.
  • delete_item — delete a child item from the configuration tree.
  • rename_item — rename an item in the configuration tree.

docs.text: • create_folder — create a folder in the configuration tree.

docs.title: Library Management
docs.text: • list_libraries, add_library, remove_library, install_library, search_libraries, uninstall_library — manage PLC library references and the local library repository.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
• build — build the TwinCAT solution.
  • get_errors — get build errors from the Error List with a severity filter.

docs.title: Solution Management
docs.text: • save_solution, new_solution, create_twincat_project, create_plc_project, close_solution — manage solutions and projects.

docs.title: Task Management
docs.text: • create_task, read_task_config, write_task_config, assign_program, remove_program — manage Real-Time Configuration tasks and program assignments.

docs.title: System Management
docs.text: • activate_configuration, start_restart_twincat, get_system_state, set_target_netid, get_target_netid, plc_login, plc_start, plc_stop, plc_logout — manage the TwinCAT runtime and target (dangerous operations are guarded).

docs.title: UserMode Runtime
docs.text:
• start_umr — start a UserMode Runtime for safe local testing (with AMS route registration).
  • stop_umr — stop the running UserMode Runtime.

docs.title: ADS Runtime
docs.text: • read_symbol, write_symbol, browse_symbols, assert_symbol — read, write, browse, and assert PLC variables at runtime via ADS.

docs.title: Safety Features
docs.text:
• Online modification guard — blocks POU code changes while the PLC is online.
  • Target safety guards — require confirmation for dangerous operations on non-UMR targets.
  • UserMode Runtime vs remote target distinction — safe operations proceed automatically on a UMR.

docs.title: Agent Connection
docs.text:
TwinCat-MCP speaks the Model Context Protocol over Streamable HTTP. Point any MCP-capable agent at the Service endpoint:

http://localhost:3001/mcp

Make sure the Service is installed and running first.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Install Claude Code if you haven't already:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

Add the MCP server:

claude mcp add --scope user --transport http twincat-mcp-service http://localhost:3001/mcp

Use --scope user

Without it, Claude Code registers the server only for the folder you ran the command in, and sessions started elsewhere won't see the tools. Check the connection with /mcp inside Claude Code.

Then start Claude Code in your TwinCAT project directory:

cd C:\MyProjects\PlcProject
claude

docs.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
docs.text:
Install the Copilot CLI via winget:

winget install GitHub.Copilot

Note

Requires a GitHub Copilot subscription (Individual, Business, or Enterprise). Open a new terminal after installation for copilot to be available.

Create or edit %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\mcp-config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "twincat-mcp-service": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3001/mcp"
    }
  }
}

Verify with /mcp show inside the Copilot CLI session. Project-level configuration is also possible at .copilot/mcp-config.json in the project root (same format).

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
Open Cursor Settings (Ctrl+Shift+J) → MCP section and add a new server:

  • Name: twincat-mcp-service
  • Type: http
  • URL: http://localhost:3001/mcp

Alternatively, add it to .cursor/mcp.json in your project root:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "twincat-mcp-service": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3001/mcp"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Once connected, your agent lists every available tool with its description. See the Tools Overview for what's on offer, Licensing to activate them, and How to Use and Best Practices before your first real task.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Shared settings live at %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP\settings.json and can be edited from the TwinCat-MCP toolbar Options button (gear icon) — a dockable, tabbed window with General, Safety & Target, Connection, UserMode Runtime and Memory & Limits pages (plus Licensing).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Description ServiceHttpPort 3001 HTTP port for the MCP endpoint. Requires a Service restart to take effect. ServicePipeName twincat-mcp-service Named pipe used by the plugin to register with the Service. HeartbeatIntervalSeconds 30 Plugin → Service keep-alive interval. RequireConfirmation true Prompt before dangerous operations on real hardware. PreferUmr false Automatically use the UserMode Runtime for dangerous tools, even without an explicit useUmr flag. CustomInstructions "" Custom prompt text sent to AI agents on connect. BrowseSymbolsMaxNodes 5000 Hard limit for one browse_symbols answer (100–20000). See Memory & Limits. MaxPrivateMemoryMB 4096 Memory guard: above this the Service restarts itself. 0 = off, otherwise at least 512.

Changing the port

If you change ServiceHttpPort, restart the Service and update your agent's endpoint URL (see Agent Connection) to match the new port.

docs.title: Memory & Limits
docs.text:
The Memory & Limits page shows the Service's memory live, like a usage meter: the bar is scaled to the memory guard, and a marker shows the estimated peak for your browse_symbols limit. It turns amber above the estimate and red near the guard. Release memory now frees unused memory immediately.

  • Browse limit (BrowseSymbolsMaxNodes): the most symbols one browse_symbols answer may contain. Agents get 1000 unless they ask for more, and they can browse deeper parts with parentPath. A higher limit allows larger answers but raises the Service's peak memory. The page shows the estimated worst case for the value you enter (about 475 MB at 5000, about 1.75 GB at 20000).
  • Memory guard (MaxPrivateMemoryMB): if the Service ever uses more than this, it logs a critical event and restarts itself (Windows restarts it within seconds; calls running at that moment fail once). This protects the workstation. The page warns you if the guard is below the estimated peak.

Both settings apply immediately, without a Service restart.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
TwinCat-MCP is installed with one MSI package that contains two features:

  • MCP Service: the TwinCatMcp Windows Service. It hosts the MCP endpoint your AI agent connects to, at http://localhost:3001/mcp. It starts automatically with Windows and needs no separate .NET runtime.
  • TcXaeShell Plugin: an extension installed into the TwinCAT XAE Shell (TcXaeShell). The Service uses it to work with your TwinCAT projects.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, and administrator rights for the installation.
  • TwinCAT 3.1 Build 4020 or later with TcXaeShell, for the Plugin. A Service-only installation does not need TcXaeShell.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download TwinCat-MCP

The button always gets the latest MSI. Older versions and the TwinCatMcp-<version>.msi.sha256 checksum files are on the TwinCat-MCP releases page.

Beta builds are not code-signed

The 0.2.0 beta MSI is not Authenticode-signed yet. Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info, then Run anyway. Before you do, check that the download is intact. In PowerShell:

(Get-FileHash .\TwinCatMcp-0.2.0-beta.1.msi -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
Get-Content .\TwinCatMcp-0.2.0-beta.1.msi.sha256

The two hashes must be the same. If they differ, do not run the file.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Run the MSI. The setup wizard shows the license agreement, then lets you choose the features (both are selected by default).

The Plugin cannot be installed while TcXaeShell is open. If it runs, setup shows a TcXaeShell is running dialog:

  • Close TcXaeShell closes it for you. TcXaeShell asks you to save unsaved changes, and setup waits up to 60 seconds.
  • Or close TcXaeShell yourself and click Retry.

If TcXaeShell runs with administrator rights, setup cannot close it; close it yourself and click Retry.

When the installation finishes, the Service is running. Open TcXaeShell to load the Plugin, then install a license: until then only the licensing tools work.

docs.title: Unattended install
docs.text:
msiexec /i TwinCatMcp-<version>.msi /qn
Property Effect ADDLOCAL=ServiceFeature Install only the Service (no TcXaeShell needed). CLOSETCXAESHELL=1 Close a running TcXaeShell during an unattended install. Without it, the install stops while TcXaeShell runs.

For example, Service only, with a log file:

msiexec /i TwinCatMcp-<version>.msi /qn ADDLOCAL=ServiceFeature /l*v install.log

A silent install skips the license page. Installing the software still means that you accept the TwinCat-MCP Standard License Agreement.

docs.title: Where things are
docs.text: What Where Service program files, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt C:\Program Files\TwinCat-MCP Plugin Extensions\TwinCatMcp in the TcXaeShell installation folder Settings %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP\settings.json (see Configuration) License files %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP\license (see Licensing)

docs.title: Port 3001 in use
docs.text: If another program already listens on port 3001, setup still installs and starts the Service and tells you which program holds the port. The Service starts listening on the configured port as soon as it is free. To use another port, set ServiceHttpPort in the Options window (TcXaeShell: Tools > Options > TwinCat-MCP, or the gear button on the TwinCat-MCP toolbar), restart the Service, and update your agent's endpoint URL.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Run the MSI of the newer version. It replaces the installed version in place and keeps your settings and license. An older MSI cannot replace a newer installed version: setup stops with "A newer version of TwinCat-MCP is already installed."

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Uninstall TwinCat-MCP from Settings > Apps, or run:

msiexec /x TwinCatMcp-<version>.msi

As with the installation, close TcXaeShell first or let setup close it.

By default the data folder %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP stays on the machine, so your settings and license are still there if you install again. To remove it as well, uninstall from the command line with PURGEDATA=1:

msiexec /x TwinCatMcp-<version>.msi PURGEDATA=1

docs.title: Verifying the install
docs.text:
The Service exposes the MCP endpoint on the local machine:

http://localhost:3001/mcp

Connect your agent (see Agent Connection) and list the available tools. If the agent sees the TwinCat-MCP tools, the Service is working. With TcXaeShell open, list_instances shows it.

docs.title: Tell the agent to use TwinCat-MCP, not the project files
docs.text:
This is the single most important rule. AI agents are file-oriented by default: when they start in a TwinCAT project folder they tend to read the .TcPOU, .TcDUT, .TcGVL, .tsproj and .plcproj files directly, grep through them, or even edit them as text. It looks like it works, but it is the wrong path:

  • Safety. TcXaeShell keeps the open project in memory. It does not notice an XML file changed underneath it, may overwrite the change on the next save, or end up in an inconsistent state (missing GUIDs, broken references, lost I/O links). The TwinCat-MCP tools change the project the same way the TcXaeShell UI does, so it always stays consistent.
  • Token efficiency. TwinCAT project files are verbose XML; a single function block file is many times larger than the Structured Text inside it. The tools return only what matters (declaration, code, structure, compact search hits), so the agent can work with a much larger project in the same context — faster and cheaper.
  • Accuracy. The tools return TwinCAT's own model: real paths, types, compile errors, runtime values. From files, the agent would have to guess.

The Service tells the agent to prefer its tools when it connects, but in practice agents still drift back to file-level work. State it explicitly, on two levels:

  1. As a standing instruction in the project's instruction file — Claude Code: CLAUDE.md in the project folder; GitHub Copilot: .github/copilot-instructions.md; Cursor: .cursor/rules — or centrally in the TwinCat-MCP CustomInstructions setting.
  2. In the request, whenever you see the agent start reading or writing files: "Don't work on the files, use the TwinCat-MCP tools."

A copy-paste instruction block (extend it with your own rules):

## TwinCAT working rules

- Work on the TwinCAT project ONLY through the twincat-mcp-service MCP tools.
  Do not read, search or edit .TcPOU, .TcDUT, .TcGVL, .TcTTO, .tsproj,
  .plcproj or .xti files directly.
- Start: launch_instance with the solution path, then project_digest or
  scan_plc_project. Use the search tool to find things, not the file system.
- Reading code: read_pou (fields=declaration or structure when you don't
  need the full code). Writing: write_pou, with dryRun=true first.
- Checking: check_objects, then build and get_errors.
- Activation, runtime and PLC operations ONLY with useUmr=true.
  Never activate or start/stop a PLC on a real target.
- Before a larger change, describe the plan and wait for approval.
- If a tool returns an error, fix it based on the error code; do not fall
  back to editing files.

docs.title: More tips
docs.text:
• Small steps. One request, one well-defined task. For bigger work ask for a plan first and only let the agent write after you approve it.
  • Use dry runs. write_pou, write_item_xml, link_variables, unlink_variables, delete_item and rename_item support dryRun to preview the change.
  • Fast feedback loop. While editing, check_objects is faster than a full build; ask for build before activation.
  • Test on the UMR, verify over ADS. Ask the agent to start the PLC on the UserMode Runtime after a change and prove the expected behaviour with assert_symbol. "It compiles" becomes "it works".
  • Review the result. Read the generated code in TcXaeShell before it goes near a real machine. A clean build does not mean the logic is right.
  • Version control. If the project is in Git, start each agent session with a clean working tree so changes are reviewable and reversible. Git operations by the agent (commit, diff) are fine — they don't conflict with the file rule above.
  • Narrow reads on big projects. Ask the agent to read only declarations, only one project's errors, or with a depth limit. See Token efficiency.
  • One solution, one TcXaeShell. Don't open the same solution in two instances (yourself and the agent). With several instances running, the agent must pass instanceId.
  • OOP code. Interfaces, properties and accessors follow a few specific rules — see Object-oriented code.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text: TwinCat-MCP is not something you operate directly. You talk to your AI agent in plain language, and the agent decides which TwinCat-MCP tools to call. Your job is to state the goal and review the result; the agent does the clicking in TcXaeShell for you.

docs.title: What it is good at
docs.text:
• Mapping and explaining an existing PLC project: which FBs, DUTs and GVLs exist and what they do.
  • Creating function blocks, methods, properties, interfaces and data types from a description.
  • Refactoring code, then building and fixing compile errors in a loop.
  • Mapping the I/O topology and linking PLC variables to I/O channels.
  • Creating and configuring tasks, assigning programs.
  • Testing on the UserMode Runtime: activate, start the PLC, read, write and assert variables.

docs.title: A typical session
docs.text:
You don't need to tell the agent these steps, but it helps to know what happens under the hood:

  1. Start an instance — launch_instance starts TcXaeShell (or reuses a running one), opens the solution and waits for the plugin to connect. Every TcXaeShell-based tool needs this first.
  2. Get oriented — project_digest or scan_plc_project maps the PLC project in one call; search finds things by name or content.
  3. Read and edit — read_pou and write_pou for declarations and code, create_pou for new items.
  4. Check — check_objects for a fast syntax check, build + get_errors for a full build; fix and repeat.
  5. Run and test — activate and start the PLC on the UserMode Runtime, then read_symbol, write_symbol, assert_symbol.
  6. Save — save_solution.

docs.title: Example prompts
docs.text:
Good first requests to try:

Open C:\Projects\Machine1\Machine1.sln and give me an overview of the PLC project: which programs, function blocks and data types exist, and what each is for.

Explain how the state machine in FB_Conveyor works, and check whether there is a branch where the motor output can stay on after a fault.

Create an FB_Debounce function block that filters a BOOL input for a given TIME. Write it, build it, and fix errors until the build is clean.

Create an interface I_Motor with a Speed : LREAL property (Get and Set) and a Start method, then an FB_Motor that implements it. Build and fix errors.

Start it on the UserMode Runtime, activate the configuration, start the PLC and verify that MAIN.nCounter is increasing.

Map the EtherCAT topology and link GVL_IO.bStartButton to channel 1 of the first digital input terminal. Show me a dry run first.

Before your first real task

Read Best Practices — especially the part about telling the agent to work through the TwinCat-MCP tools instead of editing project files.

docs.title: Safety: UserMode Runtime vs Real Hardware
docs.text: Six tools touch a running system: activate_configuration, start_restart_twincat, plc_login, plc_start, plc_stop and plc_logout. They can run against two kinds of target.

docs.title: UserMode Runtime (recommended)
docs.text:
The UserMode Runtime (UMR) is a TwinCAT runtime that runs on your engineering machine, without physical I/O. When the agent calls these tools with useUmr=true, TwinCat-MCP starts a UMR automatically (no console window) and points TcXaeShell at it. The agent can activate, start and test freely — no real machine moves.

Use get_umr_netid to get the UMR's AMS NetId for the ADS tools. You can also start the UMR manually from the TwinCat-MCP toolbar in TcXaeShell.

docs.title: Real target (default)
docs.text:
Without UMR, the behaviour depends on your settings:

  • If a UMR is already running, the operation goes there (it is the safe target).
  • If PreferUmr is enabled, the UMR is used automatically, even without useUmr=true.
  • If RequireConfirmation is enabled (default), a Windows dialog asks you to approve the operation before it reaches the real target.
  • If both are disabled, the operation runs without confirmation.

Recommended settings

Enable PreferUmr and keep RequireConfirmation on. The agent then never touches a real controller by default, and if it ever would, you have to approve it. On a real machine with a live process, do not let the agent stop the PLC or activate a configuration.

docs.title: ADS writes
docs.text: The ADS tools write to whatever target they are given. write_symbol on a UMR test is harmless; on a controller that runs a machine, only write variables deliberately and under supervision.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause What to do The agent doesn't see any TwinCat-MCP tools Service not running, wrong URL, or the server was registered for another folder only Make sure the TwinCatMcp Windows service is running, check the URL (http://localhost:3001/mcp). In Claude Code register with --scope user (see Agent Connection) and check /mcp. Every tool returns a LICENSE_* error No valid license See Licensing. NO_INSTANCE / "No TcXaeShell instance connected" No TcXaeShell with the plugin is connected Let the agent call launch_instance with the solution path, or start TcXaeShell yourself. No TwinCat-MCP toolbar in TcXaeShell Plugin not loaded Restart TcXaeShell. If that doesn't help, contact support. TIMEOUT on a long operation TcXaeShell is waiting on a dialog or is busy Check the TcXaeShell window and close any open dialog. ADS_ERROR PLC not running, or wrong target Check the PLC state; on the UMR use the NetId from get_umr_netid. A confirmation dialog pops up on activation The operation would go to a real target For UMR work enable PreferUmr (see Safety). The agent edits .TcPOU / .tsproj files directly Agents default to file-level work Tell it to use the tools; add the instruction block from Best Practices.

docs.title: Service memory
docs.text:
Large answers, mostly browse_symbols, leave buffers behind that the Service keeps for reuse. This is normal: right after many large answers the Service can use a few hundred MB. It gives the memory back by itself, every 60 s while it uses more than 256 MB, so it drops back within one to two minutes.

  • See it: Options → Memory & Limits shows the live usage, or ask the agent to call service_memory.
  • Free it now: Release memory now on that page, or service_memory with release: true.
  • Memory guard: above MaxPrivateMemoryMB (default 4096 MB) the Service logs a critical event in the Windows Application log and restarts itself. If that happens often, lower the browse limit or tell us what the agent was doing.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
When a tool fails, the agent receives a structured error with a code:

Code Meaning NOT_FOUND Path, item or file does not exist. INVALID_ARGUMENT A parameter is missing or invalid (e.g. a property without returnType). INVALID_OPERATION The operation is not possible in the current state. TIMEOUT TcXaeShell did not respond in time. ADS_ERROR ADS communication with the runtime failed. NO_INSTANCE No TcXaeShell instance is connected. ONLINE_GUARD The PLC is logged in (online); changes to code or the tree are blocked. Call plc_logout first. COM_EXCEPTION TwinCAT rejected the operation; the message has the details. INTERNAL_ERROR Unexpected error; please report it. LICENSE_* See What Licensing Gates.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
TwinCat-MCP 0.2.0 is a beta release. We know about the following and are working on them:

  • Remote Desktop. When you are logged in to the machine over RDP, launch_instance cannot start TcXaeShell (WTSQueryUserToken failed). Start TcXaeShell manually instead — the plugin connects by itself and every other tool works.
  • TwinCAT trial-license dialog. With a TwinCAT trial license, the license dialog shown on activation or UMR start can block the operation. Handle the dialog manually.
  • Missing parameters. A tool call with a missing required parameter sometimes surfaces as a generic error instead of INVALID_ARGUMENT. Agents usually retry correctly by themselves.

Still stuck? Contact info@qubernetic.com — include the time, what you asked the agent, and the error message.

docs.title: Requesting & Installing a License
docs.text: TwinCat-MCP is licensed per machine. Activating it is a two-step flow: you generate a license request on the machine that will run the Service, send it to Qubernetic, and install the token you receive back. Everything works offline; the Service never contacts a license server.

docs.title: Trial and full licenses
docs.text:
Both use the same flow and the same kind of token; only the terms and the validity period differ.

  • Trial license: for evaluating TwinCat-MCP, not for production use. It is granted under a Trial License Agreement that we sign with you, and the token is valid for the agreed trial period. To start a trial, write to info@qubernetic.com.
  • Full license: granted under the Standard License Agreement for the term of your order.

See Legal for both agreements.

docs.title: 1. Generate a license request
docs.text: The request binds your future token to this specific machine.

docs.title: From the UI (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Open the Options window from the gear "Options" button on the TwinCat-MCP toolbar.
  2. Select the Licensing page.
  3. Under "1 · Generate a license request", optionally fill in Company / Email / First name / Last name. They are embedded into the token for display only.
  4. Click Generate request. The request JSON appears in the box and is also saved to:
C:\ProgramData\TwinCat-MCP\license\license-request.json
  1. Send that JSON (or file) to Qubernetic at info@qubernetic.com to receive your token.

docs.title: Via the MCP tool
docs.text:
An AI agent (or any MCP client) can do the same with the always-available generate_license_request tool (optional params: company, email, first, last). It returns the request JSON and the saved path.

Note

The request is not secret: it only carries your machine identifier and the contact details you entered. You can share it freely.

docs.title: 2. Install your license token
docs.text: Once you receive a token (a long string starting with TCMCP1.):

docs.title: From the UI
docs.text:
1. Options → Licensing page → "2 · Install a license token".
  2. Paste the full TCMCP1.… token.
  3. Click Install license. The result line shows either:
    • Installed: the status card refreshes to Active.
    • Rejected (<STATUS>): nothing changes; see What Licensing Gates → Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Via the MCP tool
docs.text:
Use the always-available install_license tool (param: token). It returns valid, status, and a human-readable message.

Tip

Your token is validated for this machine before anything is replaced, so a rejected token never overwrites a working license.

docs.title: Where the license files live
docs.text:
The Service keeps the request and the installed license in %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP\license. Only SYSTEM and administrators can change this folder; users can read it. Install and replace tokens with the Licensing page or install_license rather than by copying files.

Uninstalling keeps this folder, so a reinstall on the same machine is licensed right away. An uninstall with PURGEDATA=1 removes it together with the rest of %ProgramData%\TwinCat-MCP (see Installation).

docs.title: Next
docs.text: See What Licensing Gates for how to check your status and what each tool needs.

docs.title: Checking your license status
docs.text:
The Licensing page (Options window) shows a license card with:

  • The licensee (company, or "First Last") and an Active / Inactive pill.
  • Valid through date with an expiry progress bar and days left.
  • The Issued date and the machine identifier (with a Copy button).
  • A Refresh button that re-queries the Service.

When there is no valid license, the card shows the reason (for example Not licensed or Service not connected).

Programmatically, the get_license_status tool returns the same data: valid, status, user_display, company/email/name, issued, expires, days_left, and a message.

docs.title: What is gated
docs.text:
With no valid license, only three operations are allowed — so you can always get yourself licensed:

  • get_license_status
  • generate_license_request
  • install_license

Every other tool is blocked until the license is valid; calls return a LICENSE_* error (see below). Starting the UserMode Runtime (UMR) is also gated: if the license isn't valid, the toolbar action shows a warning and opens the Licensing page instead of starting UMR.

docs.title: License error codes
docs.text: Error code Status Meaning LICENSE_REQUIRED MISSING No license installed. LICENSE_EXPIRED EXPIRED Past the expiry date. LICENSE_INVALID INVALID Malformed or altered token. LICENSE_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH Token was issued for a different machine. LICENSE_TAMPERED TAMPERED License integrity check failed — typically the system clock was moved backwards.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Status Cause & fix "Service not connected" — The Service isn't running or is unreachable. Make sure the TwinCat-MCP Service is up, then click Refresh. "Not licensed" MISSING No token installed. Generate a request and install a token. Rejected on install INVALID Token truncated or altered. Re-copy the full TCMCP1.… string and install again. Rejected / inactive FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH Token was issued for a different machine. Re-generate the request on this machine and request a new token. Inactive after a date EXPIRED The license expired. Request a renewed token. Inactive, "tampered" TAMPERED The system clock was moved backwards. Set the clock to the correct time and restart the Service.

Still stuck? Contact info@qubernetic.com.

docs.title: ADS (live variables)
docs.text:
These tools talk to a running PLC over ADS. They don't need TcXaeShell — only a running PLC and a reachable ADS route. Common parameters:

Parameter Description netId AMS NetId (default: current target). For the UMR use get_umr_netid. port ADS port (default 851 = first PLC runtime).

docs.title: browse_symbols
docs.text:
Lists the PLC's variables. The walk is always bounded, so even a large object graph (for example a TcOpen context) answers quickly.

Parameter Description parentPath Browse the children of this symbol (omit for the root). maxDepth Max nesting depth, default 2 (1 = only the symbols at parentPath; 0 = the hard limit of 30). maxNodes Max symbols in the answer, default 1000 (0 = the hard limit). The hard limit is the BrowseSymbolsMaxNodes setting, default 5000. followPointers Follow POINTER TO / REFERENCE TO symbols (default false). leafOnly Flat list of leaf variables only (respects maxDepth).

Symbols marked hasMore: true have children that were not expanded. Browse them with parentPath rather than raising the limits. When a limit is reached, the answer ends with a limit notice. A value above a hard limit returns INVALID_ARGUMENT with the allowed range.

docs.title: read_symbol
docs.text:
Reads a variable's current value.

Parameter Description symbolPath e.g. MAIN.bMotorRunning, GVL.nCounter.

docs.title: write_symbol
docs.text:
Writes a variable at runtime. The value is converted to the target type.

Parameter Description symbolPath e.g. MAIN.nSetpoint. value Value as string.

Warning

On a controller that runs a machine, write only deliberately and under supervision. See Safety.

docs.title: assert_symbol
docs.text:
Checks that a variable equals an expected value — the building block for automated tests on the UserMode Runtime.

Parameter Description symbolPath Variable to check. expectedValue Expected value as string.

docs.title: check_objects
docs.text:
Runs the IEC syntax check on a PLC project without a full build — much faster, ideal for the edit-check loop while writing ST code. Returns errors and warnings like get_errors. Use build before activation.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath e.g. TIPC^Plc. Auto-discovered if omitted. severity Error, Warning or Message. limit Max messages.

docs.title: build
docs.text: Builds the TwinCAT solution.

docs.title: get_errors
docs.text:
Returns the Error List after a build.

Parameter Description severity Error, Warning or Message. projectFilter Keep only entries whose project name contains this text. limit Max entries.

docs.title: save_solution
docs.text: Saves the solution.

docs.title: list_instances
docs.text: Lists running TcXaeShell and Visual Studio instances with their plugin connection status. Always available.

docs.title: launch_instance
docs.text:
Starts TcXaeShell (or reuses a running one), optionally opens a solution, and waits until the plugin has connected. Call this before any TcXaeShell-based tool. Always available.

Parameter Description solutionPath Full path to the .sln file. Omit to start an empty instance. visible Show the TcXaeShell window (default true).

Note

The solution path must be visible to the TwinCat-MCP Windows service — use a local path, not a drive letter mapped only in your user session. Over Remote Desktop, see Known limitations.

docs.title: quit_instance
docs.text:
Gracefully closes a TcXaeShell instance.

Parameter Description save Save the solution before quitting (default true).

docs.title: new_solution
docs.text:
Creates a new, empty TwinCAT solution.

Parameter Description solutionDir Directory for the new solution. solutionName Solution name, without .sln.

docs.title: create_twincat_project
docs.text:
Adds a TwinCAT XAE project to the current solution.

Parameter Description name TwinCAT project name.

docs.title: create_plc_project
docs.text:
Adds a PLC project to the current solution.

Parameter Description name PLC project name. template PLC template (default Standard PLC Template).

docs.title: close_solution
docs.text:
Closes the current solution.

Parameter Description save Save before closing (default true).

docs.title: service_memory
docs.text:
Shows how much memory the TwinCat-MCP Service uses, its memory limits, and the estimated peak for the current browse_symbols limit. With release: true it frees memory the Service no longer needs and reports before/after.

Parameter Description release Free unused memory now (default false: report only).

You rarely need it: the Service releases memory by itself. See Service memory.

docs.title: scan_io_devices
docs.text:
Scans the I/O tree and returns the hardware topology — EtherCAT master → couplers → terminals — with device types, fieldbus addresses and descriptions. Use read_item_xml on a device for channel-level detail.

Parameter Description devicePath e.g. TIID^Device 1 (EtherCAT). Omit to scan all I/O.

docs.title: link_variables
docs.text:
Links a PLC instance variable to an I/O channel. Find I/O paths with scan_io_devices and PLC variable paths with list_tree_items on the {Name} Instance node.

Parameter Description sourcePath PLC variable, e.g. TIPC^Plc^Plc Instance^PlcTask Inputs^GVL_IO.bSensor. targetPath I/O channel, e.g. TIID^Device 1 (EtherCAT)^Term 3 (EL1809)^Channel 1^Input. dryRun Preview the mapping without creating it.

docs.title: unlink_variables
docs.text: Removes a link created by link_variables. Same parameters; dryRun previews what would be removed.

docs.title: Libraries
docs.text: plcProjectPath is the PLC project path, e.g. TIPC^Plc^Plc Project.

docs.title: list_libraries
docs.text: Lists the library references of a PLC project.

docs.title: search_libraries
docs.text:
Searches the local library repository — use it after install_library to find the exact name, version and distributor for add_library.

Parameter Description namePattern Wildcards allowed, e.g. *TcoCore*. distributor Exact distributor name.

docs.title: add_library
docs.text:
Adds a library reference to a PLC project.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath PLC project path. name e.g. Tc2_Standard. version e.g. 3.3.3.0. distributor e.g. Beckhoff Automation GmbH.

docs.title: remove_library
docs.text:
Removes a library reference.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath PLC project path. name Library name.

docs.title: install_library
docs.text:
Installs a .library file into the library repository.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath PLC project path. filePath Absolute path to the .library file. overwrite Overwrite if already installed (default false). category Repository category (default System).

docs.title: uninstall_library

Removes a library from the repository.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath PLC project path. name, version, distributor Library identity; version may be *. category Repository category (default System).

docs.title: Licensing Tools
docs.text: These three tools are always available, even without a valid license, so you can always get licensed. All other tools require a valid license.

docs.title: get_license_status
docs.text: Returns the license state: valid, status, licensee, expiry, days left.

docs.title: generate_license_request
docs.text:
Generates a machine-bound license request to send to Qubernetic.

Parameter Description company, email, first, last Optional contact details shown on the license.

docs.title: install_license
docs.text:
Installs a license token (TCMCP1.…). The token is validated before anything is replaced, so a rejected token never overwrites a working license.

Parameter Description token The full token string.

See Requesting & Installing a License for the full flow.

docs.title: Tools Overview
docs.text:
TwinCat-MCP gives your agent 56 tools and 3 resources. The agent picks and parameterises the tools itself — these pages show what is possible, so you know what to ask for, and document the rules the tools follow.

Category Tools Instances & Solutions 8 Start/quit TcXaeShell, create and close solutions and projects, Service memory Project Navigation 9 Overview, search, tree browsing, XML configuration, folders, rename, delete POUs & Code 4 Create, read and write programs, FBs, methods, properties, interfaces, DUTs, GVLs Build 4 Syntax check, build, error list, save Libraries 6 References and the library repository Tasks 5 Real-time tasks and program assignment I/O 3 Hardware topology and variable links System & Runtime 10 Activation, runtime, PLC login/start/stop, target NetId, UMR ADS (live variables) 4 Browse, read, write and assert PLC variables at runtime Licensing 3 License status, request, install — always available

docs.title: Instances
docs.text: Most tools run inside TcXaeShell through the TwinCat-MCP plugin and need a connected instance: call launch_instance first (or start TcXaeShell yourself). These tools accept an optional instanceId; with a single connected instance it is resolved automatically. The ADS tools, list_instances, launch_instance and the licensing tools work without an instance.

docs.title: Tree paths
docs.text:
Items are addressed by their path in the TwinCAT configuration tree, segments separated by ^. Language-independent prefixes:

Prefix Target TIPC PLC configuration TIID I/O devices TIRT Real-time tasks TIRC Real-time configuration TINC NC configuration

A PLC project always looks like this; source code lives under {Name} Project:

TIPC
└── {Name}
    ├── {Name} Project      (POUs, DUTs, GVLs, …)
    └── {Name} Instance     (I/O mappings, task links)

Folder names such as POUs or DUTs vary per project — let the agent discover them with scan_plc_project instead of guessing.

docs.title: Token efficiency
docs.text:
Read tools return everything by default. These parameters keep answers small on big projects:

Tool Parameter read_pou fields: declaration, implementation, structure or full list_tree_items limit, compact, maxDepth browse_symbols maxDepth, maxNodes, followPointers, leafOnly get_errors projectFilter, limit, severity read_item_xml xpath, maxLength search limit

docs.title: Limits are not errors
docs.text:
When a limit is reached, the call still succeeds and the answer ends with a notice:

{"_truncated": true, "_limit": "maxNodes",
 "_message": "Limit reached, not an error: the walk stopped after 1000 symbols ..."}

_limit names the limit, _truncated is set when items were left out, and the message says how to get the rest (narrow the path or raise the named limit). The data before the notice is valid. read_item_xml marks a cut at the end of the text with [limit reached, not an error: ...].

docs.title: Dry runs
docs.text: Tools that change code or configuration — write_pou, write_item_xml, link_variables, unlink_variables, delete_item, rename_item — accept dryRun=true to preview the change without applying it.

docs.title: Online guard
docs.text: While the PLC is logged in, changes to code and the project tree are blocked with ONLINE_GUARD. Call plc_logout first.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A failed call returns a structured error the agent can branch on:

{ "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "...", "context": { ... } } }

See Troubleshooting → Error codes.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
Besides tools, the agent can read three resources without a tool call:

Resource Content plc_project_tree Compact flat list of the PLC project's tree items (name, path, type) plc_pous POUs (programs, functions, FBs, interfaces): name, type, path — no source plc_libraries Referenced libraries (name, version)

docs.title: POUs & Code
docs.text: Programs, functions, function blocks, methods, properties, interfaces, DUTs and GVLs are all created, read and written with four tools. Always edit code through these tools — never by editing .TcPOU and similar files (see Best Practices).

docs.title: create_pou
docs.text:
Creates a new item in the PLC project tree.

Parameter Description parentPath A folder for top-level items (…^POUs); the owning POU for members (…^POUs^I_Motor); the property for accessors (…^POUs^FB_Motor^Speed). name Name of the new item. Ignored for accessors, which are always named Get / Set. subType Type code, see below. language ST (default), IL, FBD, LD, SFC, CFC. returnType For functions, methods and properties, e.g. BOOL, LREAL, ST_Data. Required for properties. accessModifier PUBLIC, PRIVATE, PROTECTED or INTERNAL (methods, properties, accessors). extends Base type (FB, program, interface). implementsInterfaces Comma-separated interfaces, e.g. I_Motor, I_Diag (FB, program). declarationText Initial declaration (DUTs, GVLs).

docs.title: read_pou
docs.text:
Reads the declaration and implementation of a POU. With recursive=true it includes all methods, properties and accessors in one call.

Parameter Description path e.g. TIPC^Plc^Plc Project^POUs^FB_Motor. recursive Include all children. fields full (default), declaration, implementation or structure (names/paths only).

docs.title: read_pou_batch
docs.text:
Reads several POUs in one call; results are keyed by path, and a failure on one path does not abort the others. Same recursive and fields options as read_pou.

Parameter Description paths List of POU paths.

docs.title: write_pou
docs.text:
Writes the declaration and/or implementation of a POU in one call.

Parameter Description path POU path. declaration Full declaration text (header + VAR blocks). Omit to keep. implementation Full implementation (ST body). Omit to keep. dryRun Return current vs proposed content without writing.

docs.title: Type codes
docs.text: Code Type Code Type 602 Program 615 GVL 603 Function 616 Transition 604 Function Block 618 Interface 605 DUT Enum 610 Interface Method 606 DUT Struct 612 Interface Property 607 DUT Union 654 Interface Property Get 623 DUT Alias 655 Interface Property Set 608 Action 613 Property Get 609 Method 614 Property Set 611 Property

docs.title: Object-oriented code
docs.text:
TwinCAT has separate type codes for interface members. create_pou maps the common codes automatically based on the parent, so the agent can use the familiar ones:

Parent Requested Created as Interface Method 609 Interface Method 610 Interface Property 611 Interface Property 612 Interface Property Get 613 / Set 614 Interface Property Get 654 / Set 655 Function Block Property 611, Get 613, Set 614 unchanged

Rules worth knowing:

  • Properties are created without accessors. Add a Get (613) and/or Set (614) with the property as parentPath. This applies to interface properties too: an interface property with no accessor builds, but the syntax check warns "The property defines neither a get nor a set accessor".
  • A property needs a type. returnType is required for 611/612; without it the call fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
  • implementsInterfaces only writes IMPLEMENTS into the declaration. The interface's methods and properties are not generated — create each of them in the FB.
  • Accessor names are fixed to Get and Set; the name parameter is ignored.

A complete interface + implementation, as the agent would do it:

create_pou  parentPath=…^POUs           name=I_Motor   subType=618
create_pou  parentPath=…^POUs^I_Motor   name=Speed     subType=611  returnType=LREAL
create_pou  parentPath=…^I_Motor^Speed  name=Get       subType=613
create_pou  parentPath=…^POUs^I_Motor   name=Start     subType=609  returnType=BOOL

create_pou  parentPath=…^POUs           name=FB_Motor  subType=604  implementsInterfaces=I_Motor
create_pou  parentPath=…^POUs^FB_Motor  name=Speed     subType=611  returnType=LREAL
create_pou  parentPath=…^FB_Motor^Speed name=Get       subType=613
create_pou  parentPath=…^POUs^FB_Motor  name=Start     subType=609  returnType=BOOL  accessModifier=PUBLIC
write_pou   …  (implementations)
check_objects

docs.title: project_digest
docs.text:
One-call compact overview of a PLC project: POUs with their member names, DUTs, GVLs, referenced libraries and tasks — names, types and counts only, no source code. The best starting point for getting oriented; follow up with read_pou or search.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath e.g. TIPC^Plc. Auto-discovers the first PLC project if omitted.

docs.title: scan_plc_project
docs.text:
Maps the whole PLC project structure in one call: all folders, POUs, DUTs, GVLs and interfaces with their paths and types. Use it before navigating the tree — folder names vary per project.

Parameter Description plcProjectPath e.g. TIPC^Plc. Auto-discovers the first PLC project if omitted.

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Searches the PLC project by name or content and returns compact hits (path, kind, optional line and snippet) — never full source. Prefer it over browsing the tree or reading files when looking for something.

Parameter Description query Search text; case-insensitive substring by default. kind pou, dut, gvl, method, hardware, code, symbol or any (default). fuzzy Subsequence match, e.g. fbmot matches FB_Motor. regex Treat query as a regular expression (case-insensitive). plcProjectPath Auto-discovered if omitted. limit Max hits (default 50). netId, port Only for kind=symbol (searches live symbols over ADS).

docs.title: list_tree_items
docs.text:
Lists the children of a configuration tree node, optionally the whole subtree.

Parameter Description path e.g. TIPC or TIPC^Plc^Plc Project^POUs. recursive Include all descendants. maxDepth Recursion depth (default 10, -1 unlimited). limit Max total nodes; excess is truncated with a marker. compact Omit childCount from each node.

Each node includes its itemType (see POU type codes).

docs.title: read_item_xml
docs.text:
Reads any tree item's configuration as XML — I/O devices (TIID), tasks (TIRT), NC axes (TINC), PLC nodes (TIPC).

Parameter Description path e.g. TIID^Device 1 (EtherCAT)^Term 1 (EK1100) or TIRT^PlcTask. xpath Return only matching elements, e.g. //CycleTime. maxLength Max characters.

docs.title: write_item_xml
docs.text:
Writes partial XML configuration to a tree item. Only the elements present in the XML are applied; everything else is preserved. Read with read_item_xml first.

Parameter Description path Tree item path. xml Partial XML. dryRun Preview current vs proposed XML without writing.

docs.title: create_folder
docs.text:
Creates a folder in the project tree.

Parameter Description parentPath e.g. TIPC^Plc^Plc Project^POUs. name Folder name.

docs.title: rename_item
docs.text:
Renames a tree item.

Parameter Description path Item to rename. newName New name. dryRun Preview only.

docs.title: delete_item
docs.text:
Deletes a child item from the tree.

Parameter Description parentPath Parent containing the item. childName Name of the item to delete. dryRun Preview what would be removed.

docs.title: System & Runtime
docs.text: Tools marked touch a running system and follow the safety rules: they accept useUmr=true to run on the UserMode Runtime (started automatically if needed).

docs.title: get_system_state
docs.text: Returns the TwinCAT system state (running status) and the target AMS NetId.

docs.title: get_target_netid
docs.text: Returns the current target AMS NetId.

docs.title: set_target_netid
docs.text:
Sets the target AMS NetId.

Parameter Description netId e.g. 127.0.0.1.1.1.

docs.title: get_umr_netid
docs.text: Returns the AMS NetId of the running UserMode Runtime — use it as netId for the ADS tools.

docs.title: activate_configuration
docs.text:
Activates the TwinCAT configuration.

Parameter Description useUmr Run on the UserMode Runtime.

docs.title: start_restart_twincat
docs.text:
Starts or restarts the TwinCAT runtime.

Parameter Description useUmr Run on the UserMode Runtime.

docs.title: PLC
docs.text: plcProjectPath is the PLC project, e.g. TIPC^Plc.

docs.title: plc_login
docs.text: Logs in to the PLC runtime. While logged in, code and tree changes are blocked (ONLINE_GUARD).

docs.title: plc_start
docs.text: Starts the PLC program.

docs.title: plc_stop
docs.text: Stops the PLC program.

docs.title: plc_logout
docs.text:
Logs out from the PLC runtime.

All four take plcProjectPath and useUmr.

docs.title: create_task
docs.text:
Creates a real-time task and its PLC task reference, so programs can be assigned to it.

Parameter Description name Task name (unique). plcProjectPath PLC project for the task reference, e.g. TIPC^Plc^Plc Project. subType 0 = with process image (default), 1 = without.

docs.title: read_task_config
docs.text:
Reads a task's configuration (cycle time, priority, …) as XML.

Parameter Description taskPath e.g. TIRT^PlcTask.

docs.title: write_task_config
docs.text:
Writes a task's configuration from XML.

Parameter Description taskPath e.g. TIRT^PlcTask. xml XML configuration.

docs.title: assign_program
docs.text:
Assigns a program to a task. Build the project first so the program is registered.

Parameter Description instanceTaskPath The PLC task reference — not the TIRT task — e.g. TIPC^Plc^Plc Project^App_TaskRef. Find it with scan_plc_project or list_tree_items. programName An existing PROGRAM.

docs.title: remove_program
docs.text: Removes a program from a task reference. Same parameters as assign_program.
